title: Regular cochain and square-zero affine deformation constructions
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J$ an ideal, and $D,C$ commutative Hopf $A$-algebras, representing affine group schemes via [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $K=A/J$ and $R_0=K\otimes_A R$, the canonical presentation of $R/JR$, for any commutative $A$-algebra $R$; reduction of an algebra map is its base change. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For an augmented commutative Hopf $K$-algebra $B$, define $P_B=K\otimes_{B,\epsilon}\Omega^1_{B/K}$, where the differentials are [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and $d_e b=1\otimes db$. Put $E=\operatorname{Hom}_K(P_{D_0},K)\otimes_K(J/J^2)$; when $J^2=0$, $J/J^2$ canonically identifies with $J$. Define tensor powers recursively by $B^{\otimes0}=K$, $B^{\otimes1}=B$, $B^{\otimes(n+1)}=B^{\otimes n}\otimes_K B$ for $n\geq1$. For a $K$-module $V$, the regular cochain module is $C^n(B,V)=V\otimes_K B^{\otimes n}$. At a tuple of algebra maps $h_i:B\to T$, evaluation sends $v\otimes b_1\otimes\cdots\otimes b_n$ to $v\otimes\prod_i h_i(b_i)$. A linear coaction $\rho:V\to V\otimes_K B$ is counital and coassociative when $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_V$ and $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$, with the canonical tensor associators and unitors; its action at $h:B\to T$ sends $v\otimes t$ to $\sum v_i\otimes h(b_i)t$ when $\rho(v)=\sum v_i\otimes b_i$. On group points use convolution of algebra maps and inversion by composition with the antipode. Define $\operatorname{Ker}_R$ to be the points $g:D\to R$ whose reduction equals the identity point. A comparison family consists of bijections $\kappa_R:E\otimes_K R_0\simeq\operatorname{Ker}_R$ for flat $A$-algebras $R$; no additivity, naturality or normalization is assumed by this type. For $f:D\to C$, the predicate $\operatorname{HasDefect}(\kappa,f,c)$ says that for every flat test algebra $R$ and $h,k:C\to R$, $\kappa_R(c(h_0,k_0))=f(hk)f(k)^{-1}f(h)^{-1}$. For $b\in E\otimes_K C_0$ and flat $C$, define the actual correction coordinate map by the convolution product $\operatorname{correct}(\kappa,f,b)=\kappa_C(b)f$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Appendix B.2, regular Hochschild cochains pp.283--284, Proposition B.2.5 and Corollary B.2.6 pp.286--287; explicit affine tensor presentations.
